question: In a patient with phaeochromocytoma, a beta-blocker can be safely started before alpha-blockade because cardioselective agents like atenolol do not affect vascular β2 receptors.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. The alpha-first rule in phaeochromocytoma is absolute. Beta-blockade before adequate alpha-blockade — even with a 'cardioselective' agent — can precipitate a hypertensive crisis by removing the β2-mediated vasodilatory counterbalance to massive α1 vasoconstriction from tumour catecholamines.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. The alpha-first rule is absolute: beta-blockade before alpha-blockade removes the vasodilatory β2 counter-pressure against tumour catecholamines, leaving pure α1-mediated vasoconstriction unopposed — precipitating a life-threatening hypertensive crisis. Even cardioselective agents lose selectivity at higher doses. Always establish alpha-blockade first (phenoxybenzamine 10–14 days pre-op).
